question: Should Gateway allow scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if so should that live in existing `allowedOrigins` syntax or a constrained pattern field?
rationale: The request changes browser-origin authorization for Gateway WebSocket clients, and current related PRs show demand but do not establish the permanent wildcard grammar or security posture.

options.title: Define a constrained pattern contract
options.body: Add reviewed pattern semantics, tests, docs, and audit behavior for extension/custom-scheme origin patterns instead of accepting arbitrary trailing-prefix wildcards.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Review or land exact opaque-origin fixes and close the changing-extension-ID wildcard behavior as outside the current Gateway origin policy.

options.title: Allow only `chrome-extension://*`
options.body: Support the minimal requested syntax, but require narrow scheme-only matching and negative security tests before merge.

recommendation.title: Define a constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Add reviewed pattern semantics, tests, docs, and audit behavior for extension/custom-scheme origin patterns instead of accepting arbitrary trailing-prefix wildcards.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest history on the Gateway browser-origin hardening boundary and explicit-origin requirement.
